post.caption:
Moravec's paradox: reasoning is computationally cheap, perception and dexterity are extremely expensive. Evolution spent hundreds of millions of years on moving through a physical world and only a sliver on abstract thought, so the things you do without noticing are the hard ones. A towel has no fixed shape, has folds you cannot see, and changes as you grip it. A chess board does not. Which flips the usual prediction about which jobs are safest.
